what: The coarse pattern everyone learns first
title: Reading isotopic fine structure
text: Start compound whose isotope pattern needs explaining: diclofenac, C₁₄H₁₁Cl₂₂, anti-inflammatory drug common enough urinary xenobiotic turns untargeted metabolomics data. Two chlorines give textbook barcode.  Diclofenac’s isotope pattern unit resolution. what: What is actually inside methionine’s M+2
title: Reading isotopic fine structure
text: isotope_fine_pattern() doesn’t stop nominal sum — every row one isotopologue, exact mass, labelled isotopes produced : Every isotopologue methionine default 0.01% threshold, enviPat. Plotted directly m/z axis — Da scale spectrum viewer uses, milli-Da rescaling — M+1 M+2 regions split several distinct peaks:  Methionine, M+1: five candidate isotope substitutions, spread across 0.009 Da. Carbon dominates, almost every organic ion.  Methionine, M+2: 34S alone outweighs every carbon-combination roughly 40-fold, exactly matching excess spotted coarse pattern . Two things coarse bar chart never show visible . First, sulfur’s +2 isotope physically sits apart every carbon-based explanation — 13C, 13C (two different carbons, ¹³C) sits 0.01091 Da away 34S, large enough gap two genuinely different masses, two names peak. Second, height difference sulfur signal: 34S towers every combination carbons, nitrogens oxygens also reach +2, fine-structure version 40-fold excess already spotted coarse pattern — now specific competing hypothesis (¹³C¹³C) sitting specific, different mass, instead vague “something else.”
code: pat_met %>% arrange(desc(abundance)) %>%   mutate(mz = round(mz, 5), abundance = round(abundance, 4),          label = ifelse(label == "", "M (monoisotopic)", label)) %>%   knitr::kable(caption = "Every isotopologue of methionine above the default 0.01% threshold, from enviPat.") plot_level <- function(pattern, level, title) {   base <- pattern$mz[pattern$label == ""]   d <- pattern %>% mutate(nominal = round(mz - base)) %>% filter(nominal == level) %>%     mutate(element = sub(",.*", "", label), element = sub("^[0-9]+", "", element),            col = ifelse(label == "" | grepl(",", label), "combo", element),            col = ifelse(col %in% names(COL), col, "combo"))   ggplot(d, aes(mz, abundance, colour = col)) +     geom_segment(aes(xend = mz, y = 0, yend = abundance), linewidth = 2.2, lineend = "round") +     geom_text(data = slice_max(d, abundance, n = min(6, nrow(d))),               aes(label = label), angle = 90, hjust = -0.15, size = 3.1, colour = "grey20") +     scale_colour_manual(values = COL, guide = "none") +     scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_number(accuracy = 0.0001)) +     scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .35))) +     labs(x = "m/z (Da)", y = "% of M (monoisotopic)", title = title) +     theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +     theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) } plot_level(pat_met, 1, "Methionine M+1") plot_level(pat_met, 2, "Methionine M+2")

code: R_at_mz <- function(mz, R_ref, mz_ref = 200) R_ref * sqrt(mz_ref / mz)  Rs <- c(15000, 60000, 120000) R_label <- function(r) sprintf("R = %s @200", format(r, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)) pat_met2 <- pat_met %>% mutate(nominal = round(mz - base_met)) %>% filter(nominal == 2)  prof <- bind_rows(lapply(Rs, function(r)   isotope_profile(pat_met2, resolution = R_at_mz(mean(pat_met2$mz), r)) %>%     mutate(R = R_label(r)))) ticks <- pat_met2 %>% filter(abundance > 0.02)  ggplot(prof, aes(mz, intensity)) +   geom_area(fill = BLUE, alpha = .25) +   geom_line(colour = BLUE, linewidth = .8) +   geom_rug(data = ticks, aes(x = mz), inherit.aes = FALSE, sides = "b", colour = "grey30", linewidth = .6) +   facet_wrap(~ factor(R, levels = vapply(Rs, R_label, "")), ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +   scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_number(accuracy = 0.0001)) +   labs(x = "m/z (Da)", y = "simulated intensity (% of M)") +   theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +   theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), strip.text = element_text(hjust = 0))

title: Simulating isotope fine structure for a formula
text: isotope_fine_pattern() wraps enviPat enumerate every isotopologue formula threshold, labelled isotopes produced . Swap candidate formula : Every isotopologue C14H11Cl2NO2 default 0.01% threshold. Grouping nominal mass reproduces coarse M/M+1/M+2 pattern calculator give — diclofenac’s two chlorines make one unambiguous even unit resolution:  Diclofenac’s coarse isotope pattern: two chlorines produce textbook M/M+2/M+4 barcode.
code: formula <- "C14H11Cl2NO2"   # diclofenac -- replace with your own candidate  pat <- isotope_fine_pattern(formula) pat %>% arrange(desc(abundance)) %>%   mutate(mz = round(mz, 5), abundance = round(abundance, 4),          label = ifelse(label == "", "M (monoisotopic)", label)) %>%   knitr::kable(caption = paste("Every isotopologue of", formula, "above the default 0.01% threshold.")) base_mz <- pat$mz[pat$label == ""] coarse <- pat %>% mutate(nominal = round(mz - base_mz)) %>%   group_by(nominal) %>%   summarise(mz = base_mz + first(nominal), abundance = sum(abundance), .groups = "drop")  ggplot(coarse, aes(mz, abundance)) +   geom_segment(aes(xend = mz, y = 0, yend = abundance), colour = BLUE, linewidth = 2.2,                lineend = "round") +   geom_text(data = filter(coarse, abundance > 1), aes(label = paste0("M+", nominal)),             vjust = -0.6, size = 3.4, colour = "grey25") +   scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .15))) +   labs(x = "m/z (Da)", y = "relative abundance (%)") +   theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +   theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

what: Step 3 — would your instrument resolve the candidates?
title: Simulating isotope fine structure for a formula
text: every pair isotopologues nominal level, resolving power needed put valley (m1+m2) / 2 / |m1-m2| m/z; translated usual Orbitrap convention (quoted reference m/z, typically 200), scales 1/sqrt(m/z): Every pair M+2 candidates 0.01% abundance, resolving power (quoted m/z 200, Orbitrap convention) separate . 37Cl needs R ~ 28,769 m/z 200 separate closest competitor (13C, 2H) – trivially available current Orbitrap.
code: R_at_mz  <- function(mz, R_ref, mz_ref = 200) R_ref * sqrt(mz_ref / mz) fwhm_at  <- function(mz, R_ref, mz_ref = 200) mz / R_at_mz(mz, R_ref, mz_ref)  ## every pairwise gap within one nominal level, and the resolving power (at the ## reference m/z used above) that would put a valley between the peaks. Faint ## candidates (< min_abundance percent) are dropped so the table stays a short, ## readable list of comparisons an analyst could actually be faced with. separations <- function(pattern, level, R_ref = 120000, mz_ref = 200, min_abundance = 0.01) {   base <- pattern$mz[pattern$label == ""]   d <- pattern %>% mutate(nominal = round(mz - base)) %>%     filter(nominal == level, abundance >= min_abundance) %>%     mutate(label = ifelse(label == "", "M", label))   if (nrow(d) < 2) return(tibble())   ix <- combn(seq_len(nrow(d)), 2)   bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(ncol(ix)), function(i) {     ra <- d[ix[1, i], ]; rb <- d[ix[2, i], ]     sep_da <- abs(ra$mz - rb$mz)     Rreq <- (ra$mz + rb$mz) / 2 / sep_da                       # R needed AT that m/z     Rref_req <- Rreq / sqrt(mz_ref / mean(c(ra$mz, rb$mz)))    # translated to the R_ref convention     tibble(a = ra$label, b = rb$label, abundance_a_pct = round(ra$abundance, 3),            abundance_b_pct = round(rb$abundance, 3), separation_Da = round(sep_da, 5),            R_needed_here = round(Rreq), R_needed_at200 = round(Rref_req))   })) %>% arrange(R_needed_at200) }  sep2 <- separations(pat, 2) sep2 %>%   knitr::kable(col.names = c("a", "b", "abundance a %", "abundance b %",                               "separation (Da)", "R needed here", "R needed @200"),                caption = "Every pair of M+2 candidates above 0.01% abundance, and the resolving power (quoted at m/z 200, Orbitrap convention) that would separate them.") top <- sep2 %>% filter(a == "37Cl" | b == "37Cl") %>% slice_min(R_needed_at200, n = 1) cat(sprintf("`37Cl` needs only R ~ %s at m/z 200 to separate from its closest competitor (`%s`) -- trivially available on any current Orbitrap.",             format(top$R_needed_at200, big.mark = ","), ifelse(top$a == "37Cl", top$b, top$a)))

what: Fine isotopologue pattern for a molecular formula — isotope_fine_pattern
title: Fine isotopologue pattern for a molecular formula — isotope_fine_pattern
text: Wraps enviPat::isopattern() compute exact fine isotopic structure neutral molecular formula: every isotopologue combination threshold, exact mass abundance relative monoisotopic (base) peak. Unlike nominal-mass isotope pattern (M, M+1, M+2, ...), resolves individual contributors within nominal level – e.g. M+2 satellite sulfur-containing compound really 34S isotopologue (13C, 13C) isotopologue sitting two different exact masses, function tells apart.

title: Fine isotopologue pattern for a molecular formula — isotope_fine_pattern
code: isotope_fine_pattern(formula, threshold = 0.01, charge = 0)

title: Fine isotopologue pattern for a molecular formula — isotope_fine_pattern
text: formula molecular formula string, e.g. "C5H11NO2S". threshold minimum abundance keep, percent base peak. charge charge state passed enviPat::isopattern(). applies electron-mass correction intrinsically charged species (e.g. metal ion); add proton adduct. simulate ion [M+H]+, leave charge = 0 (default, .e. neutral formula's pattern) add adduct's mass difference mz afterwards, e.g. pattern$mz + 1.007276 protonation – massdiff convention used MZ_CAMERA.

title: Fine isotopologue pattern for a molecular formula — isotope_fine_pattern
text: tibble columns mz, abundance (percent   base peak, 100 = tallest) label, human-readable isotope   label built isotope composition isotopologue (e.g.   "34S", "13C, 13C"; "" monoisotopic peak).

what: Simulate a resolving-power-dependent profile from a fine isotope pattern — isotope_profile
title: Simulate a resolving-power-dependent profile from a fine isotope pattern — isotope_profile
text: Sums Gaussian peak appropriate width isotopologue isotope_fine_pattern result, chosen resolving power. low resolving power, isotopologues close mass merge one apparent peak; high resolving power separate – Orbitrap FT-ICR spectrum ion actually looks like. abundance already expressed percent base peak, overlapping isotopologues sum way real overlapping peaks , simulated apex can exceed single isotopologue's abundance.

title: Simulate a resolving-power-dependent profile from a fine isotope pattern — isotope_profile
code: isotope_profile(pattern, resolution = 120000, oversample = 12, pad_fwhm = 6)

title: Simulate a resolving-power-dependent profile from a fine isotope pattern — isotope_profile
text: pattern output isotope_fine_pattern (tibble(mz, abundance)). resolution resolving power (R = m/z / FWHM) m/z pattern. instrument's resolving power quoted reference m/z (usual Orbitrap convention, typically 200), convert first, e.g. R_ref * sqrt(200 / mean(pattern$mz)). oversample grid points per FWHM. pad_fwhm many FWHM m/z padding add side.

title: Simulate a resolving-power-dependent profile from a fine isotope pattern — isotope_profile
text: tibble columns mz intensity (percent   base peak's abundance, scale isotope_fine_pattern()'s   abundance column).

what: Look up an observed m/z difference against the theoretical differences table — mz_diff_lookup
title: Look up an observed m/z difference against the theoretical differences table — mz_diff_lookup
text: interpretation workhorse behind "delta ": given mass difference measured two peaks spectrum (-source fragment, homologous-series step, suspected adduct...), returns every entry mz_diff_table within tolerance.

title: Look up an observed m/z difference against the theoretical differences table — mz_diff_lookup
code: mz_diff_lookup(   delta,   tol = 100,   unit = c("ppm", "Da"),   mode = c("both", "pos", "neg"),   table = mz_diff_table(match.arg(mode)) )

title: Look up an observed m/z difference against the theoretical differences table — mz_diff_lookup
text: delta observed difference, Da. tol tolerance. ppm delta default (usual way instrument's mass accuracy quoted); switch unit = "Da" flat window instead. Note ppm DIFFERENCE, either peak's m/z – small delta can unrealistically tight window (10 ppm 1 Da delta 0.00001 Da), since true uncertainty difference comes peaks' mass accuracy, size gap . Widen tol accordingly, pass absolute unit = "Da" tolerance already know window want. unit "ppm" (default) "Da". mode passed mz_diff_table table supplied. table table mz_diff_table; computed automatically mode omitted. Pass avoid recomputing calling repeatedly (e.g. every peak pair spectrum).

title: Look up an observed m/z difference against the theoretical differences table — mz_diff_lookup
text: table, filtered rows within tolerance delta,   added error_Da column, sorted abs(error_Da).

title: Look up an observed m/z difference against the theoretical differences table — mz_diff_lookup
text: Jan Stanstrup, stanstrup@gmail.com

title: Reference table of theoretical m/z differences — mz_diff_table
text: Combines commonMZ's adducts_fragments repeating_units_pos/repeating_units_neg tables one tibble tagged category ionisation mode, comparing difference measured two peaks spectrum every known adduct/fragment/repeating-unit mass difference . See mz_diff_lookup filter specific observed difference.
